name: argo-events-b3af946b-blind26-ots
instr:
# A Kubernetes event-driven automation platform gives inverted answers everywhere, without a test suite

I run a platform that takes in notifications from outside systems and fires things off in response, and since the last sync of this build almost everything I do comes back not merely wrong but frequently the exact opposite of what it used to be. The repository has received 26 separate undocumented edits. They show up both when I hand in configurations for approval and when data actually flows through a running deployment.

Handing in intake configurations is where I noticed it first. A subscription definition for a topic-based streaming broker that plainly lists two topics is turned away with the complaint that the topic list cannot be empty, while a completely blank definition of that kind is waved through and no longer reports the empty topic list at all. A filled-in definition for a queue-style message broker, host and topic both present, is refused because a topic must be given; a lightweight telemetry-broker definition with an address and a topic is refused the same way, and that in turn poisons a combined definition mixing a log-streaming feed with a telemetry feed, which is now rejected as a whole even though the names are unique and the update strategies agree. A definition that points at its connection address through a secret reference is refused as if it carried no address whatsoever, while one carrying neither an address nor a secret reference no longer prompts
